findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-7 success; cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers (CAP-7) > Cross-engine lock
findings.issue: The CAP-7 success criterion (both browser:<engine> phases start before either ends) is met even when the lock serializes everything. On bankwire, the universal smoke and 4 of the 5 specs have a BO goto, so they take the lock exclusive. The only FO-only spec, checkout-empty-banks, can overlap only with the other engine's copy of itself. The two browser phases therefore 'overlap' only as wall-clock spans, while the scenarios run almost fully serialized. Meanwhile every parallel boot adds snapshot-db plus lock-wait overhead.
findings.implementation_impact: CAP-7 can pass its test and still make the bankwire release gate slower than sequential browsers (snapshot-db + lock-wait + extra worker processes). Nothing in the contract detects this, and the before/after timing report would show it only after the code is built.
findings.suggestion: Change the CAP-7 success criterion to measure real concurrency, e.g. the summed scenario run time of both engines is greater than the version's wall-clock for browser driving, or lock-wait totals stay below a stated share of browser time. Also state the expected CAP-7 benefit on bankwire given its BO-heavy specs, or add a rule that falls back to sequential browsers when most scenarios are BO, to skip the snapshot-db cost.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Success signal; cell-contract.md > Phase timings (CAP-6) last bullet; cell-contract.md > Aggregate
findings.issue: The success signal takes the 'after' wall-clock of one fix-loop iteration from CAP-6 e2e_phase_durations. But the aggregate builds e2e_phase_durations only from the records it selected for the verdict: the newest gate-grade record, else the newest record. A warm fix-loop iteration is never gate-grade, so once any cold record exists for the cell, its timings never reach e2e_phase_durations. The 'before' side relies on progress-log START/END timestamps, but the progress log is truncated on every run (run-phases.md, cell-contract.md Phase timings). No step says when or how the baseline gets captured before the scripts change.
findings.implementation_impact: The mandatory before/after report cannot be produced from the named sources. Implementers will either invent an ad-hoc extraction, or measure after the upgrade, when the 'before' scripts no longer exist.
findings.suggestion: Name the source for warm-iteration timings (e.g. read phase_durations/boot_phases of the specific record from the cell history, not the aggregate). Add an explicit step: capture the 'before' numbers on bankwire with today's scripts before any script change lands, copying each progress log after each run. Define the measured unit for both sides (which layers count as part of a 'fix-loop iteration', image already pulled, same --jobs/slots, same host load).

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers (CAP-7) > Parallel-only failures ('So no DB row, file, cache or opcode state written by the parallel pass can be confirmed as a failure')
findings.issue: The rerun-seq reset deletes files that are absent from the snapshot, recopies modules/<mod>, and clears var/cache. It does not restore docroot files that existed at the snapshot and were modified by the parallel pass (e.g. .htaccess regenerated by a BO setting, theme or config files, overwritten images). The Warm container section admits this exact gap ('Files that existed at baseline and were modified are not restored'), but the CAP-7 text claims complete isolation. Also, rerun-seq does not re-run the module install. A failure that depends on install-time side effects that the parallel pass mutated is therefore not reset either.
findings.implementation_impact: A finding produced by residue from the other engine's parallel pass can be 'confirmed' by rerun-seq and block the release gate. That breaks the identical-findings guarantee, and the live test will flake on modules whose BO scenarios rewrite existing files.
findings.suggestion: Either state the same limitation as for the warm reset and weaken the CAP-7 'identical to sequential' claim, or extend the snapshot to record checksums (or mtime+size) of pre-existing docroot files and restore modified ones from a copy taken at snapshot time.

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-7 success ('findings are identical to a sequential run'); cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers > Identical findings, Slots
findings.issue: The reference 'sequential run' is undefined in a way that matters. In the --sequential-browsers fallback (and today's runner), the second engine runs on the DB that the first engine already mutated, with no reset between engines. In parallel mode, each failing engine is confirmed from a clean snapshot. bankwire relies on cross-engine state: checkout-with-bank's description says the second engine's add-bank POST fails duplicate validation and the checkout uses the first engine's bank row, and checkout-empty-banks assumes zero banks. So the outcome for engine 2 depends on the mode. Whether a version is admitted parallel or sequential depends on free slots, i.e. on host load.
findings.implementation_impact: The same module and source can get different findings, and a different ready, depending on how many slots were free at admission. The identical-findings live test compares two modes with different state semantics, so it can fail or pass for reasons unrelated to the implementation.
findings.suggestion: Define the sequential reference precisely (e.g. sequential mode also resets to the post-warmup-bo snapshot between engines), so both modes give each engine the same starting state. Apply that reset in the --sequential-browsers fallback too, and say so in cell-contract.md.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers > Parallel-only failures ('rerun failures the parallel pass did not report, are added to inconclusive'); cell-contract.md > Plan step 3 blocked-infra
findings.issue: A failure that appears only in the sequential rerun is a conclusive, reproducible defect that the parallel pass hid (e.g. by FO-FO overlap or state from the other engine). The contract files it under `inconclusive`, so the cell becomes a pass with non-empty inconclusive (reason inconclusive-steps). Plan step 3 treats inconclusive-steps as an infra cause. Two such runs in one session give `blocked-infra`, which ends the E2E loop and reports a real module bug as an infrastructure problem.
findings.implementation_impact: Real defects get mislabeled as infra and never enter findings. The operator is told to fix infrastructure, and the E2E loop stops without a loop-back to fix the bug.
findings.suggestion: Give rerun-only failures their own channel (e.g. `sequential_only`) and a non-infra plan reason. Or treat a conclusive rerun failure as a blocking finding: it was produced sequentially from a clean snapshot, which is the confirmation standard the contract itself sets. Exclude that cause from blocked-infra.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers, second bullet (BO-login fallback '#2' pass); SPEC.md > Constraints ('Release-gate evidence comes only from cold boots') and Assumptions ('warm state can mask install-path bugs')
findings.issue: When one engine's BO login fails in parallel mode, its result is discarded and replaced by a '#2' pass run after an in-place reset (reset-db/reset-files/reset-opcache, no reinstall). 'Only that pass counts, its findings need no sequential confirmation', and the record keeps boot: cold, so it is gate-grade. This is exactly the reset-container evidence that the constraints forbid for the gate (warm-like state, install not re-run). The record carries no marker that would let the plan or aggregate tell it apart.
findings.implementation_impact: Release-gate evidence for a cell can come from a reset container rather than a cold boot, with no field that exposes this. That undermines the honesty law that the spec puts first.
findings.suggestion: Mark such records (e.g. `boot: cold-reset` or a `reset_pass: true` field) and decide explicitly whether they are gate-grade. If not, have the plan schedule a cold single-browser run for that cell instead of accepting the #2 pass.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers > Cross-engine lock ('The wait has no timeout of its own'); references/headless.md (silence rule); run-phases.md (SLOW rule)
findings.issue: lock-wait:<engine> has no deadline. If the holding engine hangs inside a scenario (crashed renderer, a Playwright driver hang, browser.close() blocking), the waiting engine waits forever and the version process never finishes. Both phases keep emitting ALIVE/SLOW heartbeats, so the headless '3 minutes without new line' stop rule never fires, and headless policy for SLOW is 'wait'. wait-slots for cells queued behind the run's own cells is also explicitly unlimited. Neither phase gets a SLOW threshold, so interactive runs will flag routine waits as 'suspected stall' after 180 s and offer to kill the job.
findings.implementation_impact: A headless gate run can hang indefinitely. Interactive runs produce false stall alarms during normal tier-1 queueing and BO serialization, which pushes the operator toward stopping healthy jobs.
findings.suggestion: Give lock-wait a bound derived from the holder's remaining scenario budget (or a per-worker overall deadline enforced by the version process, which kills the hung worker and records `crash`). Add per-phase SLOW thresholds (or exempt the phases) for wait-slots, lock-wait and rerun-seq in PROGRESS_SLOW_AFTER_PHASE, and update the stall guidance in run-phases.md and headless.md.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Constraints (Headless) and tier-matrix.md > Rules ('stops at the first step that is not clean'); cell-contract.md > Configured cells / psm_e2e_canary
findings.issue: The canary is fixed (newest version × chromium) and does not adapt to the host. If the canary cell cannot run for infra reasons (chromium binary missing, the 9.1 image absent while headless never pulls, a 9.1-only boot problem), tier 0 is never clean. Headless then returns at once and interactive ends in blocked-infra after two attempts. No other configured cell runs, even when its image and browser are available. Today the same run would still produce Firefox evidence and evidence for the other versions.
findings.implementation_impact: Headless callers (psm-develop, psm-cross-version) get zero E2E evidence on any host where the canary cell has an infra problem, which is a regression in information compared to the current runner. Operators can only work around it by editing psm_e2e_canary by hand.
findings.suggestion: Define a canary infra fallback: when the canary's newest record is inconclusive for an environment reason (browser-unavailable, missing image / errors before install), the plan picks the next configured cell as the acting canary for that session and reports it. Or at least state the regression and add the canary-unavailable case to the headless return contract.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Headless (return JSON gains versions, not_run_cells, e2e_tier_reached; early returns are status: complete); cell-contract.md > Docs to update at implementation
findings.issue: The headless return contract changes meaning. A call now stops at the first unclean tier step and reports other versions as `not reached: stopped at <step>`. Each call mints a new session, so blocked-infra never fires across calls. The 'Docs to update' list covers only the cleanup-orphans part of references/headless.md (its Kembalian section is not listed). It names none of the four callers (psm-develop, psm-cross-version, psm-scaffold, psm-optimize), whose fix loops interpret the result.
findings.implementation_impact: Callers keep reading the old per-version verdict semantics. A caller may treat `not reached` versions as failing (or passing), or loop forever re-calling psm-validate on a persistent infra cause, because every call starts a fresh session.
findings.suggestion: Add references/headless.md 'Kembalian' (new fields, the not-reached meaning, the one-step-per-call behaviour) and each caller skill that consumes the verdict to the update list. State how a caller should react to `not reached` and repeated infra reasons across calls (e.g. pass the session token back in, or have the caller stop after N identical infra returns).

findings.location: SPEC.md > CAP-1 intent; tier-matrix.md > Rules (Phase 1 loop ends only when V is clean); cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 1, Phase 2 entry
findings.issue: Phase 2 (tier 1, Layer 3, aggregate) starts only when every version is clean on Layers 1, 2 and 5 and tier 0 is gate or done. The only escape is 'E2E loop ended'. There is no defined exit for a blocking Layer 1/2/5 finding, or a canary E2E failure, that the operator cannot or will not fix in this session (false positive, accepted incompatibility, fixture problem). Today the operator can move on to Phase 2 and get an honest ready=false verdict with full evidence. Under this contract the interactive session never reaches the aggregate.
findings.implementation_impact: Interactive sessions can deadlock in Phase 1 with no verdict file, no tier-1 evidence and no Layer 3 review. Implementers will add an undocumented operator bypass, which then has no defined effect on ready, the hosting loop or the session state.
findings.suggestion: Define an explicit operator 'stop converging' action: it ends the loops, runs the Phase 2 steps that are still meaningful (Layer 3, merge-only, aggregate), records the stopped state the way 'E2E loop ended' does, and keeps ready=false. Also say whether tier 1 runs in that case.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > Storage (append-only <module>-e2e-<ver>-<browser>.jsonl)
findings.issue: Histories are append-only and never compacted or rotated. Every plan call (several per fix-loop iteration) and every aggregate call parses every line of every configured cell's history, and each record carries findings, screenshots lists, boot_phases and keeper_boot. Over months of fix loops on one module, the files and the parse cost grow without bound. Nothing defines retention, or which records a compaction may safely drop given the 'newest gate-grade', 'recorded failure' and 'latest full-scenario record' rules.
findings.implementation_impact: Plan latency and disk use grow over time. A later ad-hoc cleanup that drops old lines could silently change derivations: losing the failing record changes the focus cell, and losing the latest full record changes the failed set.
findings.suggestion: Specify a compaction rule that keeps, per cell, the records every derivation can still select (newest record, newest gate-grade, newest cold full conclusive, newest conclusive, latest full-scenario, the last two records for blocked-infra) and drops the rest, run under the same LOCK_EX. Or set a retention bound and test that compaction does not change any plan output.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers > Cross-engine lock (FO-only scenarios shared) and Parallel-only failures (only engines with findings are rerun)
findings.issue: Only engines that reported findings get rerun-seq. A scenario that passes in the parallel pass because the other engine's persistent writes changed its preconditions is never re-examined. The lock prevents overlap, not ordering-dependent state. On bankwire, whether engine B's checkout-empty-banks ('0 banks, early-return path') runs before or after engine A's checkout-with-bank adds a bank depends on scheduling. So the zero-bank path is exercised or skipped nondeterministically, and the record cannot show which happened.
findings.implementation_impact: A cell's passing gate-grade evidence may not have covered the behavior its spec claims to cover, and the coverage differs from run to run. That is a false pass the honesty law is meant to exclude.
findings.suggestion: Either reset to the post-warmup-bo snapshot per engine before each engine's first scenario that the other engine's BO writes could affect (simplest: run engines on separate DB copies, or separate shops/schemas), or document the limitation and require specs whose preconditions are global (e.g. 'no banks') to declare it, e.g. a spec field that forces sequential, reset-isolated execution.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Plan > steps 5-7 (cold-version, cold-canary, focus); SPEC.md CAP-1, CAP-4, CAP-5
findings.issue: A warm or failed-only run passes while the following cold full run fails on the same source_fingerprint, for example because of residue in a file modified since baseline (which warm reset does not restore), an install-path bug, or a scenario-order dependency that `requires` does not declare. The derivation then cycles with no patch in between: the cold fail gives a recorded failure, so `focus` runs warm. The warm pass makes the newest fresh conclusive record a pass, so `cold-canary`/`cold-version` runs. The cold fail starts the cycle again. `blocked-infra` covers only inconclusive causes, so nothing ends the cycle.
findings.implementation_impact: The plan keeps the loop going while every warm iteration reports green. The operator sees no failure to fix, and the E2E loop never ends or reaches the gate.
findings.suggestion: Add a rule: when a cell's newest cold full conclusive record is `fail` and a newer warm or partial `pass` has the same source_fingerprint as that fail, step 7 sets e2e_warm=false and e2e_scenarios=full (or reports a dedicated cause such as `warm-cold-divergence`), so the next focus run is cold and full and the fix loop sees the real failure. Add a test: cold fail, warm pass, cold fail on one fingerprint derives a cold full focus, not a third cold-canary/cold-version.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Warm container > Chain / Owner (keeper started with start_new_session, own warm Job ID)
findings.issue: ps-run-layer is stopped (via `--stop-job` on its own Job ID, SIGTERM, or Ctrl-C) while it waits for a just-started keeper to write session.json. The keeper sits in its own session under a different Job ID, and the orchestrator does not know that Job ID yet, because it is printed only at attach. The contract does not say whether stopping ps-run-layer also stops the keeper, or what record the cell gets.
findings.implementation_impact: The keeper keeps booting and holds a slot. The next warm call finds no session.json, starts a second keeper for the same (module, version, owner), and breaks the at-most-one-keeper rule. Two containers then hold slots until the TTL runs out.
findings.suggestion: State that ps-run-layer prints and logs the warm Job ID as soon as it spawns the keeper, and that its stop handler sends `--stop-job <warm-id>` to a keeper it started whose session.json does not exist yet (the cell gets `stopped`). Also take a per-(module, version, owner) start lock, or write a `starting` marker under `<tmp>/psm-warm/` before spawning, so a concurrent or later lookup waits for that keeper and does not start another.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Warm container > Chain ("waits for the session file until the keeper exits") and Reset per iteration (phase `baseline`)
findings.issue: The wait for session.json is bounded only by the keeper's pull, bring-up and wait-healthy timeouts. The `baseline` phase (a `--databases` dump plus the docroot file list) comes after wait-healthy and has no timeout of its own. During that whole wait the keeper logs only to its own `-warm.progress.log`, and nothing says ps-run-layer writes heartbeats to the version progress log the orchestrator tails.
findings.implementation_impact: A hung dump blocks ps-run-layer forever. A normal keeper boot leaves the version log unchanged for 3 minutes or more, so the run-phases stall rule (b) reports a false stall.
findings.suggestion: Give `baseline` a timeout (for example the op timeout or `psm_flashlight_startup_timeout`); on expiry the keeper exits and the cell gets `keeper-start`. Specify that ps-run-layer logs a `keeper-wait` phase with `ALIVE` heartbeats every 15 s in the version progress log, naming the warm log path, while it waits.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers > Cross-engine lock (`lock-wait:<engine>`, no timeout) and Config keys > psm_e2e_slots (`wait-slots` without limit when queued behind own cells); references/run-phases.md SLOW threshold of 180 s
findings.issue: The contract makes `lock-wait:<engine>` and own-run `wait-slots` unbounded on purpose, but these phases fall under the general SLOW rule (180 s). With a shared `LOCK_SH`/`LOCK_EX` flock, which has no fairness guarantee, an engine can wait through many of the other engine's BO scenarios. The contract exempts the keeper idle wait from the stall rule (`ALIVE idle`) but not these two phases.
findings.implementation_impact: A healthy parallel gate run logs `SLOW lock-wait` or `SLOW wait-slots`. The orchestrator then reports a suspected stall to Budi and offers to stop a run that is making progress.
findings.suggestion: Specify that `lock-wait:*` and own-queue `wait-slots` emit `ALIVE` heartbeats naming the holder or blocking cells and are exempt from the SLOW threshold, or get a SLOW threshold derived from the holder's remaining scenarios. Update the run-phases.md token table to match.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 1 (hosting version) and Run scope; tier-matrix.md Rules (tier 0 runs inside the hosting version's loop)
findings.issue: The operator's run scope (`--versions`) excludes the hosting version, for example scope 8.1 while the canary is 9.1:chromium. The contract does not say whether the hosting loop still runs Layers 1, 2 and 5 for that out-of-scope version, whether it is skipped, or what ends it. Its E2E step is `blocked-by-scope`, which ends the E2E loop, but its own L1/2/5 cleanliness is still required for the loop to end.
findings.implementation_impact: The orchestrator may run Docker layers on a version the operator excluded, or wait for a loop that never starts. Phase 2 entry behavior also diverges between implementations.
findings.suggestion: Specify that when the hosting version is outside the run scope, no Phase 1 loop runs for it: the orchestrator takes the E2E plan call once, which reports `blocked-by-scope` and ends the E2E loop, and only in-scope versions run Phase 1 loops. Alternatively, define the hosting version as the first in-scope version. Add a test with scope 8.1 and canary 9.1.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > State, freshness, gate-grade > Fresh (excludes `psm_reports_dir` "when it lies inside it")
findings.issue: `psm_reports_dir` equals the module root, or the module directory lies inside `psm_reports_dir`. The exclusion rule covers only a reports dir strictly inside the module, so these boundary cases are not specified.
findings.implementation_impact: If the module root itself is excluded, the fingerprint covers no files and never changes. Old pass records then stay fresh after any patch, and `ready` is wrongly true.
findings.suggestion: Make it an input error (exit 2) when `realpath(psm_reports_dir)` equals the module root or is an ancestor of it. Exclude it only when it is a strict descendant. Add a test.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Configured cells ("Gating without E2E stays possible only through `ps-aggregate.py --require` without `e2e`") vs Plan > E2E loop ended ("gating by `--require` without `e2e` ... never a pass and `ready` stays false")
findings.issue: The two passages conflict when gating uses `--require` without `e2e`. One keeps a way to gate without E2E. The other says `ready` stays false once the E2E loop has ended for that reason.
findings.implementation_impact: The aggregate either never allows `ready` without E2E, which removes the documented `--require` escape, or lets it through against the honesty text. Tests and the orchestrator report will disagree.
findings.suggestion: Reword E2E loop ended to say: `e2e` is never a pass and the E2E portion of `ready` stays false, but when `--require` excludes `e2e`, the aggregate's `ready` ignores E2E cells (reported as not required) as today. Add an aggregate test for `--require static,flashlight,scenario` with no E2E records.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > "Newest / latest = highest `started_at`, ties broken by `run_id`"; Plan focus cell / recorded failure / has-passing-gate-grade selection
findings.issue: Record order depends only on wall-clock `started_at`. On the stated WSL2 host the guest clock can drift and then jump backward after host sleep or resync. A later record can then carry an earlier `started_at` than the record it supersedes. The append order in the history file, which is monotonic, is not used.
findings.implementation_impact: An older gate-grade `pass` can be selected over a newer `fail`, so `ready` is wrongly true, an honesty-law violation. Focus cell and newest-run selection can also point at the wrong cell.
findings.suggestion: Order a cell's records by line position in its append-only history (each append is atomic under `LOCK_EX`). Use `started_at` only to order across cells, for example to find the newest run, or add a monotonic sequence field written under the lock. State this, and add a test where a newer line has a smaller `started_at`.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 1 / Phase 2 entry
findings.issue: Version V is 'clean' only when phase1_reuse is true AND its Layers 1, 2 and 5 hold no blocking finding, and Phase 2 entry requires that 'one --per-version plan call ... must show every version clean'. But ps-plan-layers.py only judges freshness (reuse/rerun, phase1_reuse); no field anywhere (plan or aggregate) reports 'no blocking finding on L1/2/5 per version'. The plan call that is supposed to show cleanliness cannot show it.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must either invent a new plan field (and decide which layer files and which finding severities count as blocking) or leave the orchestrator to judge blocking findings by reading layer JSON by hand, which SKILL.md forbids ('jangan nilai ulang'). The Phase 2 entry check and the hosting-loop exit condition cannot be tested as written.
findings.suggestion: Define a plan output, e.g. per_version[V].clean (phase1_reuse plus no blocking finding in V's per-version static/flashlight/scenario files, judged by ps-aggregate's existing layer functions), plus a top-level phase2_ready, and state that the orchestrator gates on these fields. Add a unit test for both.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Config keys > Image tag; Aggregate
findings.issue: Plan, runner and aggregate must resolve image tags the same way: resolve_tag(parse_tag_map(--tag-map else psm_flashlight_tag_map; --extra-tag-map)). ps-aggregate.py has no --tag-map or --extra-tag-map flag today. The spec lists only --config and --session as new aggregate flags, and says only that ps-run-layer takes the two flags from its passthrough.
findings.implementation_impact: When the operator uses --extra-tag-map (which SKILL.md allows), the aggregate resolves a different tag from the one the runner recorded. Every cell then reads stale-tag and ready stays false with no error. The implementer has to guess whether to add the flags or to ignore the case.
findings.suggestion: State that ps-aggregate.py gains --tag-map and --extra-tag-map, with the same semantics as the plan's. Also state that the orchestrator passes the same values to plan, ps-run-layer passthrough and aggregate. Alternatively, forbid --extra-tag-map for runs that gate on E2E.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md > Rules > Visual review
findings.issue: Pending visual entries must be tagged with 'the run's source_fingerprint', and at merge time entries with a stale fingerprint are dropped. No script exposes a fingerprint to the orchestrator. ps-run-layer's output line carries only e2e_status, reason and appended. The plan output does not list the current fingerprint.
findings.implementation_impact: The orchestrator (a model) would have to read raw .jsonl history lines to tag entries, and would have to compute a SHA-256 over the module tree itself to judge staleness. That is error-prone and is the kind of manual judgment the skill forbids.
findings.suggestion: Have ps-plan-layers.py emit source_fingerprint (current), and have ps-run-layer's final JSON line include the fingerprint it computed before admission. Then refer to both fields in the visual-review rule.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Headless; tier-matrix.md > Rules (headless stops at first step not clean)
findings.issue: Headless 'drives the plan's steps in order and returns at the first step that is not clean'. Tier 0 runs inside the hosting (canary) version's Phase 1 loop, which runs first. The spec does not say whether the Phase 1 loops of the other versions (Layer 2 flashlight and Layer 5 scenario per-version runs) still run before returning when the canary E2E step fails. Read literally, they do not. The later '--merge-only for Layers 2 and 5' then finds no per-version files for 1.7.8 and 8.1.
findings.implementation_impact: Under the literal reading, a headless caller such as psm-develop gets no Layer 2 or 5 verdict for the non-canary versions whenever the canary E2E is red. A Layer 2 install error on 1.7.8 stays hidden until E2E is fixed. The implementer must pick between two orchestration orders that give callers very different results.
findings.suggestion: State explicitly whether headless finishes every version's Phase 1 (Layers 1/2/5, which do not depend on E2E) before honouring the E2E stop, or whether it skips them. If they are skipped, state how unreached Layer 2/5 versions are reported in the return JSON.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Warm container > Chain / Pre-iteration check
findings.issue: The keeper is started as 'ps-e2e-run.py --keep-warm --warm-ttl ... --warm-owner <token>' and the iteration as a child with --use-warm. The spec does not say which passthrough flags each one receives: --allow-image-pull, --orchestrator, --db-image, --ps-domain, --startup-timeout, --timeout, --tag-map/--extra-tag-map, --admin-path/--admin-email/--admin-password, --nav-timeout, --screenshot-dir, --headed. The pre-iteration check compares only keeper liveness, health, image tag, module path and version. It does not compare db-image, orchestrator, ps-domain or admin settings.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must guess how the flags are split. Without --allow-image-pull or the right tag map the keeper may fail to boot, which wrongly disables warm mode for the whole session (keeper-start). If settings change between iterations, a mismatched container is silently reused.
findings.suggestion: List which flags go to the keeper (boot-time: orchestrator, db-image, ps-domain, startup-timeout, timeout, tag maps, allow-image-pull, admin-path) and which go to the iteration (admin credentials, nav-timeout, screenshot-dir, headed). Record the boot-time ones in session.json and add them to the pre-iteration mismatch check.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Warm container > Chain (keeper-start record)
findings.issue: 'A keeper that exits first gives the cell an inconclusive record, reason keeper-start, with the keeper's errors and boot_phases.' The keeper writes session.json only after wait-healthy and baseline succeed. No channel is defined for the keeper to hand errors or boot_phases to ps-run-layer when it dies during pull, bring-up or wait-healthy.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer cannot fill errors or boot_phases on the keeper-start record without inventing a result file or a stderr protocol. The CAP-6 timings for failed keeper boots would be lost.
findings.suggestion: Specify a keeper result file, e.g. <tmp>/psm-warm/<warm-id>/exit.json or an -o path passed by ps-run-layer, that the keeper writes on every exit path. Define its shape: errors, boot_id, boot_phases, wall_clock.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Success signal (before/after timing report)
findings.issue: The mandatory before/after report is not operationally defined. 'Before' is to come from progress-log START/END timestamps of the current scripts, but no such logs exist for the 2026-09-08 bankwire run: _bmad-output/psm-validate has no bankwire *.progress.log, and logs are truncated every run. So a fresh baseline run with the current scripts must be made before any script is changed. The spec does not define the 'before' fix-loop iteration (which command: ps-run-layer --layer e2e --versions 9.1 with which browsers? with the injected fault?) or the 'before' release gate (--jobs 3, both browsers, all three versions?). It also does not say where the report is written or in what format.
findings.implementation_impact: A required done-criterion cannot be produced or checked reproducibly. If the implementer starts editing scripts first, the 'before' baseline can no longer be measured with the current code.
findings.suggestion: Add a short procedure covering: (1) the git commit or tag of the 'before' scripts; (2) the exact before and after commands for one fix-loop iteration and for the full gate on a temp copy of bankwire, with the same injected fault; (3) the report path and a JSON or Markdown shape (per phase, per boot, wall-clock). Also note that the baseline must be captured before the first script change.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Success signal vs cell-contract.md > Plan > Phase 1 (hosting loop)
findings.issue: The hosting loop runs the E2E step 'only once V is clean'. A patch stales V's Layers 2 and 5 by mtime, so every fix-loop iteration first re-runs a cold flashlight boot and a cold scenario boot for V, each with bring-up and wait-healthy, before the warm E2E run. The success signal ('a fix-loop iteration ... completes as a warm canary run with no pull, bring-up or wait-healthy phase') only holds if 'iteration' means the E2E run's own progress log.
findings.implementation_impact: The structural success check and the 'one fix-loop iteration' wall-clock in the timing report can be read two ways: E2E only, or the whole loop iteration including the Layer 2 and 5 cold boots. The two readings give different pass/fail outcomes and different speed-up numbers.
findings.suggestion: State that the success signal and the timing report measure (a) the E2E run only, or (b) the full hosting-loop iteration including Layers 1/2/5. If (b), say whether the Layer 2/5 boots are expected to appear.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers > Cross-engine lock (Test)
findings.issue: 'Test: on bankwire with two engines, the logged runs of every BO scenario overlap no scenario of the other engine.' No per-scenario log line or record field is defined: only browser:<engine> and lock-wait:<engine> phases exist. Progress-log timestamps use isoformat(timespec='seconds'), so sub-second boundaries cannot prove or disprove overlap.
findings.implementation_impact: The test cannot be written against the specified artefacts. The implementer must invent a per-scenario phase or field and choose a time resolution.
findings.suggestion: Define a per-scenario phase (e.g. scenario:<engine>:<name>) or per-scenario started_at/finished_at with monotonic or millisecond timestamps in the worker result, and assert non-overlap on those values.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers ('two concurrent BO sessions with the same admin work on every target version')
findings.issue: The pass criterion of this live test is undefined. It could mean both logins return authed, or both sessions are still authed after the other engine logs in, or each can load an authenticated BO page and run a BO action after the other's login. It is also unclear whether a failure on one version blocks the implementation or only triggers the runtime fallback.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer cannot write a deterministic assertion. On PrestaShop versions that invalidate the older session, a weak criterion would pass while BO steps become inconclusive or masked at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Specify the sequence: login A, login B, then A and B each load a named authenticated BO page (e.g. AdminModules&configure=bankwire) and assert an authed marker. Also state what a failure on a given tag means: CAP-7 disabled for that version, or a test failure.

findings.location: tier-matrix.md > Rules > Loop-back vs cell-contract.md > Plan steps 5-7
findings.issue: Tier-matrix describes each loop-back as focus, then cold-version V, then cold-canary, then gate, and says a failure in step 2 or 3 restarts at step 1. In the plan derivation, step 6 (cold-canary) requires 'no non-canary cell is failing'. With two failing cells from one gate run, the derived order is focus A, cold-version A, focus B, cold-version B, cold-canary. Tier-matrix step 3 is skipped for A, which the matrix text does not describe.
findings.implementation_impact: An implementer or test author following tier-matrix would expect a cold-canary between the two loop-backs, contradicting the plan test 'two failing cells from one tier-1 run walk through both loop-backs'.
findings.suggestion: Amend the tier-matrix Loop-back rule: 'with several failing cells, steps 1-2 repeat per failing cell; step 3 runs once after no non-canary cell is failing', or give the expected step sequence for the two-cell test explicitly.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Plan > step 3 blocked-infra (cause list)
findings.issue: The infra causes are 'reason of an inconclusive record other than stopped, or inconclusive-steps (non-empty inconclusive) or browser-notes for a pass that is not passing gate-grade'. In rerun_matrix, browser-notes is a catch-all ('any other gate-grade pass that is not passing gate-grade', which also covers scenario_notes that differ from the current notes). Here it may mean literally non-empty browser_notes. The rule also does not say whether non-gate-grade passes (warm or partial) produce a cause, or are ignored.
findings.implementation_impact: Under one reading, two consecutive same-session records (for example a warm partial pass followed by a cold pass with differing scenario_notes) trigger blocked-infra and end the E2E loop. Under the other they do not. That changes when ready can ever become true in a session.
findings.suggestion: Enumerate the cause key per record kind, e.g. inconclusive -> reason; gate-grade pass with non-empty inconclusive -> inconclusive-steps; gate-grade pass with non-empty browser_notes -> browser-notes; anything else -> no infra cause. Add a test where a warm pass followed by a cold pass does not give blocked-infra.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Headless vs .claude/skills/psm-validate/references/headless.md
findings.issue: The spec says every early return (step not clean, blocked-*, E2E skipped) is status: complete with ready: false, and that blocked is reserved for 'cannot assess at all'. headless.md says that when the log is silent for about 3 minutes without DONE, the run stops its job and returns blocked with a reason. Under the new contract a stopped job yields an inconclusive/stopped record, i.e. a step that is not clean, which should be complete. The 'Docs to update' entry for headless.md mentions only the automatic --cleanup-orphans. It omits the new return fields (versions{e2e_state,reason}, not_run_cells, e2e_tier_reached), per-call --new-session minting, the headless config copy, stop-at-first-not-clean, and no-warm.
findings.implementation_impact: Two documents give conflicting return statuses for a stalled job. The headless contract that callers read would not describe the new fields or stop rule.
findings.suggestion: Decide which status a stopped or stalled job returns under the new contract, and extend the headless.md entry in 'Docs to update' with every headless change listed in cell-contract.md > Headless.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Constraints (headless callers keep their per-version verdict contract) vs .claude/skills/psm-optimize/SKILL.md (Verifikasi)
findings.issue: psm-optimize judges compatibility as a per-version delta against its baseline validate status ('tak ada kegagalan baru dibanding sebelum'). With headless stop-at-first-not-clean, a module whose canary is already red at baseline leaves 1.7.8 and 8.1 'not reached' in both the baseline and the after run. A new regression on those versions is then invisible. The claim that callers keep their per-version verdict contract changes meaning for this caller, and psm-optimize is not in 'Docs to update'.
findings.implementation_impact: After the change, psm-optimize can declare 'no new failures' while two of three versions were never tested. This is a silent honesty gap in a sibling skill.
findings.suggestion: Add psm-optimize (and, if relevant, psm-develop and psm-cross-version) to 'Docs to update': a version with reached: false is not comparable and must not count as 'no new failure'. Alternatively, let callers request continue-past-failure for baseline runs.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Aggregate (configured set vs existing --versions)
findings.issue: ps-aggregate.py today takes target_versions from --versions or, when absent, from the static payload's versions, and uses them for every layer and for compute_ready. The spec says the aggregate reads the configured set from --config for E2E. It does not say whether --config also sets target_versions for the non-E2E layers, or what happens when --versions or the static scan's versions differ from psm_target_versions. Headless claims 'ready and versions cover exactly the caller's cells'.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must choose whether versions[...] and the non-E2E part of ready follow --versions, the static payload, or the configured set. A mismatch could leave a configured version absent from versions[] while E2E still requires it, or the reverse.
findings.suggestion: State that the aggregate's target versions equal the configured psm_target_versions (from --config). State whether --versions narrower than that set is an input error or report-only, and how the static payload's versions are checked against it.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Entry points / Runner input errors (existing tests and quickstart)
findings.issue: The contract makes ps-aggregate.py --e2e an input error, has the aggregate ignore <module>-e2e*.json, and makes --per-version and --jobs input errors for --layer e2e. The current suites use these paths heavily: about 24 e2e references in test-ps-aggregate.py, 21 in test-ps-run-layer.py and 9 in test-ps-plan-layers.py. e2e-quickstart.md's TDD loop ends with 'ps-aggregate.py --static ... --e2e e2e.json'. The spec does not say whether these tests are rewritten against histories or deleted. It also does not say what replaces the quickstart's verdict step: a direct ps-e2e-run.py output is 'never evidence', and plan calls now need --session.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must decide test migration without guidance. 'Suite green' is not a usable done-signal while existing assertions encode the old contract, and the quickstart flow has no verdict path.
findings.suggestion: Add a line to brownfield.md or cell-contract.md: existing tests for e2e file I/O are migrated to the history format (list the behaviours to keep), and the quickstart's verdict step becomes '<what command>'. Add --session to the quickstart and adversarial-lens doc updates.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Evidence record > session (--new-session)
findings.issue: 'ps-plan-layers.py --new-session (prints a random [a-z0-9]{16} and exits)'. module_path is a required positional argument of ps-plan-layers.py today. The spec does not say whether --new-session is allowed without it, or is mutually exclusive with the other flags.
findings.implementation_impact: This is a small guess, but it shapes the On Activation command in SKILL.md and headless.md.
findings.suggestion: State: --new-session takes no module_path, conflicts with every other flag (exit 2), prints only the token to stdout and exits 0.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > State, freshness (shared fingerprint function)
findings.issue: 'Plan, runner and aggregate share one function' for source_fingerprint, but no owning script is named. For the shared normalizer, by contrast, the spec says explicitly 'in ps-flashlight-run.py next to CONFIG_KEY_TO_DEST'. The aggregate already loads ps-plan-layers.py as a sibling, and ps-run-layer loads ps-aggregate.
findings.implementation_impact: This is a minor guess. A wrong placement creates an import cycle or a second implementation, which the project's 'one owner' rule forbids.
findings.suggestion: Name the owner, e.g. ps-plan-layers.py (source_fingerprint(module_dir, reports_dir)), consumed by ps-aggregate via the existing load_sibling and by ps-run-layer via aggregate().

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Config keys > psm_e2e_slots ('docker ps --filter label=psm.slots, with the op timeout')
findings.issue: It is unclear which 'op timeout' applies. ps-run-layer has no timeout flag. ps-flashlight-run.py's DOCKER_CMD_TIMEOUT (120 s) bounds short docker commands, while the children's --timeout (default 600 s) is the per-version operation timeout.
findings.implementation_impact: This is a minor guess. A 600 s timeout per admission count would stall admission for 10 minutes on a hung daemon before 'counts as cap full'.
findings.suggestion: Say 'DOCKER_CMD_TIMEOUT (120 s)', or name the passthrough flag to use.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Parallel browsers > BO-login fallback and Parallel-only failures
findings.issue: Both mechanisms run after all workers exit, each with a full reset to the snapshot. The spec does not define how they are ordered or combined when one version has an engine whose BO login failed (its #2 pass counts and 'needs no sequential confirmation') and another engine with findings (rerun-seq). It is unclear whether each sequential pass gets its own reset, whether the #2 pass's own findings also get a rerun-seq, and in what order the engines run, which matters for {browser} data and for the #2/#3 suffixes.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer must invent the ordering. Different orderings change which findings are confirmed, the boot_phases suffixes, and the wall-clock.
findings.suggestion: Specify the post-parallel sequence: e.g. for each engine in psm_e2e_browsers order, first the BO-login fallback pass if needed, then rerun-seq for engines with findings, each preceded by a full reset. Also give the {browser} expansion for the fallback pass.

findings.location: cell-contract.md (top) > identical-findings test and success-signal fixture
findings.issue: The fault is 'one authored spec's expect_text is changed so it fails on every engine'. In bankwire only checkout-with-bank.json has expect_text: two in BO (steps 4 and 17, conclusive only when bo_authed) and four in FO (steps 45 and 54-56). The file and step are not named.
findings.implementation_impact: If a BO expect_text is chosen, a flaky BO login turns the fault into an inconclusive step. The identical-findings test's 'non-empty confirmed set' then fails for reasons unrelated to CAP-7. Two implementers would build different fixtures.
findings.suggestion: Name the fixture exactly, e.g. checkout-with-bank.json step 55 (FO 'Please send us your payment by bank transfer') changed to a non-matching text, with the success signal's one-line patch restoring it.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Warm container > Teardown ('The orchestrator stops it when the loop ends')
findings.issue: It is unclear which loop is meant: the hosting Phase 1 loop, the E2E loop ending (blocked-*, skipped), or the end of the psm-validate session. A keeper is also stopped automatically before any non-warm e2e run, so the orchestrator's own stop duty is ambiguous.
findings.implementation_impact: This is a minor guess. A keeper may hold a host-wide slot for up to 60 minutes after interactive validation ends, which shows up as no-slots for other sessions.
findings.suggestion: State: the orchestrator runs --stop-job on its own keepers when the hosting loop ends and at session end, including when the E2E loop ended early.

findings.location: SPEC.md > Assumptions (canary = newest target x Chromium) vs source request
findings.issue: Budi asked for 'version 9 + Chrome first'. The spec maps this to 'newest of psm_target_versions x chromium', i.e. Playwright's bundled Chromium, not branded Google Chrome. If targets later include 10.0, the canary silently moves away from 9. Both are reasonable readings, but they are recorded only as an assumption, and the verbatim source is not kept (frontmatter sources: []).
findings.implementation_impact: The impact is low. The implementer will use chromium/newest, but Budi may expect the Chrome channel or a pinned 9.x.
findings.suggestion: Confirm with Budi, or state explicitly: 'Chrome' = Playwright chromium engine (no Chrome channel), and canary = newest configured version, not pinned to 9.x. Optionally quote the source request in Why.
